clue.text: This person is receiving new South African politician and cricketer

indicators.note: to receive something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the setter speaking of himself: 'I am'
N is the standard abbreviation for new
P. W. Botha, apartheid-era South African prime minister and president

explanation.surface: Someone takes in a rookie South African who is both a politician and a cricketer.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion splits I AM between its A and M rather than between the two words. 'Politician and cricketer' looks like one person, but only the cricketer is defined.
explanation.definitionFit: Ian Botham is the famous England all-rounder of the 1980s, one of English cricket's best-known players.

clue.text: Barely dared talk of regions

indicators.note: something done barely is stripped right down, so each word loses its outer letters and keeps its core

parts.note: the inside of the word, without its first and last letters
the inside of the word, without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone hardly had the nerve to discuss local areas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barely' reads as an adverb on 'dared', but it strips both following words to their middles.
explanation.definitionFit: Areal is the adjective from area, describing things relating to an expanse of land or surface.

clue.text: Servant in terrible trouble having lost ring

indicators.note: something terrible is in a dreadful state, so the letters are thrown into disorder
having lost something means it is no longer there, so a letter drops out

parts.note: taken as written
a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A servant is in serious bother after losing a ring, perhaps one he was meant to look after.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the O out of TROUBLE, then rearrange the six remaining letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A butler is the chief manservant of a household, in charge of wine and serving at table.

clue.text: Tapeworm again eating up hosts

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from the bottom back to the top
a host holds guests within, so the letters sit inside the run of words

parts.note: the letters straddling the two words, read in clue order

explanation.surface: A tapeworm, back once more, feeding on the animals that carry it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hosts' fits a parasite so well it looks like the definition's partner, but it is the signal that the letters are held within.
explanation.definitionFit: Taenia is the zoological genus name for common tapeworms, used as a word for the worm itself.

clue.text: Unpleasant Head of Legal gets removed

indicators.note: the head is the leading letter, singled out here as the part that is to go
something removed is taken away, so the singled-out letter disappears

parts.note: a synonym: permitted by law

explanation.surface: A nasty head of a legal department is sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of Legal' looks like a job title, but it asks for the first letter of a word meaning legal, and 'gets removed' deletes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Awful and unpleasant are everyday synonyms, both describing something bad or disagreeable to experience.

clue.text: Who strutted in, incredibly eccentric?

indicators.note: something incredible is beyond belief, a sign the letters will not stay as given

parts.note: the three words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone asks who swaggered into the room looking so bizarre.
explanation.walkthrough: The question reads as gossip about a flamboyant entrance; all thirteen letters of the first three words are the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Round the twist is British slang for crazy or mad, a colourful way of calling someone very odd.

clue.text: Having some luck in Scrabble, or getting nowhere?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: picking a blank tile from the bag, a wildcard that can stand for any letter
second meaning: failing to find what one is looking for

explanation.walkthrough: In Scrabble the two blank tiles are the most valuable to pick up, so the literal action is lucky while the idiom means failure.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally describes pulling a wildcard tile and idiomatically means having no success or no ideas.

clue.text: Communist president on live radio initially introduced by rubbish actor

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it, so the pieces sit side by side
introduced into something means put inside it, here by the word that does the enclosing

parts.note: rot is nonsense or rubbish
to be is to exist, to live

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
red is the traditional label for a communist
Gerald Ford, the 38th US president

explanation.surface: A communist leader appears on live radio, introduced by a terrible actor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On live radio' suggests a broadcast, and 'Communist president' a single leader; in fact the colour and the US president are separate pieces placed after the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Redford is the American film star of Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid and The Sting.

clue.text: Red meat and game outsiders nicked from racecourse

parts.note: lamb is a meat
RU stands for rugby union, the game

indicators.note: nicked means stolen, so the outside letters of the course's name are taken away

parts.note: Ascot is a famous English racecourse, home of Royal Ascot

explanation.surface: Red meat and game birds, with outsiders, horses unlikely to win, stolen from the races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red meat' looks like one phrase, but Red alone is the definition. ASCOT, an English racecourse, loses its outer letters to give SCO.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambrusco is a sparkling Italian red wine, so 'red' stands for it as wine drinkers use the word.

clue.text: Extremely catty row about award for play

indicators.note: to be about something is to go round it, so these letters surround another piece
the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only those letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word
a row is a line
MBE, Member of the Order of the British Empire, a British honour

explanation.surface: A really spiteful quarrel breaks out over a prize for a stage play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row about award' tempts you to put the award inside the row alone, but the two ends of 'catty' join the row to form the outer shell. MBE is a British honour from the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Cymbeline is one of Shakespeare's late romances, about a legendary king of ancient Britain.

clue.text: Tube strikes both the left and right wing declare void

indicators.text: strikes both the left and right wing
indicators.note: strikes means deletes, and the left and right wings are the outer letters at each end

parts.note: a cannula is a thin tube inserted into the body by doctors

explanation.surface: London Underground strikes, backed by left and right alike, declared void.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is the London Underground in the surface, but here it is a medical tube; striking its two wings removes C and A.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul a marriage or contract is to cancel it officially, as if it never had legal force.

clue.text: Painter's blue line

parts.note: feeling blue is feeling down or depressed
RY is short for railway, a rail line

explanation.surface: An artist's characteristic use of a blue stroke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Painter's blue' sounds like a pigment, but the 's is 'is', and blue means sad.
explanation.definitionFit: L. S. Lowry was an English painter known for scenes of industrial northern towns with matchstick figures.

clue.text: Taken aback, see you cuddling hot Buddhist

indicators.note: taken back means carried in the backward direction, so the letters run right to left
to cuddle is to hug, wrapping arms round something held inside

parts.note: ta-ra is an informal British goodbye, like 'see you'
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone is startled when a farewell turns into a hug from an attractive Buddhist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken aback' reads as surprised but is the reversal signal. Ta-ra is a northern English way of saying goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: An arhat is a Buddhist who has attained enlightenment, a perfected saint in Theravada tradition.

clue.text: Sign of god protecting India

indicators.note: to protect something is to shield it, keeping it safely surrounded

parts.note: Ares is the Greek god of war
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An omen showing that the gods are watching over India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign of god' reads as a divine portent; 'of' is only the link and the sign is astrological.
explanation.definitionFit: Aries, the Ram, is the first sign of the zodiac, so it is a sign in the astrological sense.

clue.text: African language that's funny supported by America

indicators.note: in a down clue, what is supported sits on top, with its support below it

parts.note: ha is a laugh at something funny
the abbreviation for the United States of America

explanation.surface: A comic African language that gets American backing.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'supported by' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Hausa is a Chadic language spoken widely in northern Nigeria and Niger, a major West African lingua franca.

clue.text: Pronoun in London and Surrey etc?

wordplay.note: places located in England's south-eastern region, written with the definite article plus the compass abbreviation

explanation.surface: Asking which pronoun people use in London and the Home Counties.
explanation.walkthrough: London and Surrey are both in the South East of England, so they are in THE SE. Surrey is a county just south-west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: These is a demonstrative pronoun, the plural of this, pointing to things nearby.

clue.text: Recovered gambler

definitions.meaning: first meaning: well again after an illness
second meaning: one who places wagers

explanation.walkthrough: The two words look like one phrase about an addict in recovery; each is a separate meaning of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has got over an illness is said to be better, and a person who bets is literally a better.

clue.text: Mix socially with tramp visited by northern bishop

indicators.note: with means alongside, so the pieces are set next to each other
a visitor comes inside, so one piece enters another

parts.note: a hobo is a homeless wanderer
N is the abbreviation for northern
B is the chess notation abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: Socialising with a vagrant, who receives a visit from a bishop from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Visited by northern' puts N inside HOBO, and the bishop's B follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To hobnob is to mingle informally, especially with people of higher social standing.

clue.text: Harden cover without using sulphur

indicators.note: doing without something means leaving it out, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: to cover against risk is to insure
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: Toughening a protective coating without any sulphur, like a chemist hardening a surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harden cover' looks like a process applied to a coating; 'cover' is a policy word for insurance.
explanation.definitionFit: To inure someone is to accustom them to hardship until they are toughened and no longer feel it.

clue.text: Discomfort when a French telecoms company rings

parts.note: un is French for 'a' with a masculine noun

indicators.note: to ring something is to encircle it, so these letters go round another piece

parts.note: EE is a British mobile network operator
as and when both mean at the time that

explanation.surface: Feeling uneasy when a French phone company keeps calling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rings' plays on phone calls from a telecoms firm; it actually means encircles. EE is a UK mobile phone network.
explanation.definitionFit: Unease is a feeling of anxiety or discomfort, the noun for not being at ease.

clue.text: Missionary type occasionally bores king of Israel

indicators.note: to bore into something is to drill inside it

parts.note: Saul was the first king of Israel in the Bible

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: the first and third letters of the word

explanation.surface: A preacher of a certain sort sometimes wearies a biblical king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missionary type' looks like the definition, but 'type' supplies letters. Fittingly, Saul was also the apostle's name before his conversion.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul the Apostle made great missionary journeys round the Mediterranean, spreading early Christianity.

clue.text: Finishing early, raced to insulate a cold room

indicators.note: insulation wraps round something, so these letters enclose another piece
finishing early means stopping before the end, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: sped is the past tense of speed, to race
taken as written
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone hurried to insulate a chilly room before finishing ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold room' looks like a unit, but 'cold' gives C and 'room' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Room and space are synonyms for available capacity, as in 'no room' or 'no space' left.

clue.text: Youngster of mine bored by golfer on a regular basis

indicators.note: something bored by a drill has another piece driven inside it

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: One of my children is regularly bored stiff by a golfer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Youngster of mine' reads as my child, but 'mine' is a pit and 'bored' means drilled into.
explanation.definitionFit: A piglet is a young pig, so it is a youngster of the animal world.

clue.text: On speed, caught sleeping around? Absolutely not!

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
haste is speed or hurry

explanation.surface: Someone on drugs caught being promiscuous indignantly denies it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On speed' suggests amphetamines, but 'speed' is just a synonym and 'On' places the cricket C above it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being chaste means abstaining from sex, the very opposite of being promiscuous, so the denial defines it.

clue.text: Libido's back — you and I credit nurses and shrink

indicators.note: to nurse is to cradle or hold close, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

indicators.note: a word's back is its tail end, so only its final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word
you and I together are we

explanation.surface: Sex drive returns; a couple credit a therapist who nurses them along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shrink' looks like a psychiatrist alongside the libido, but it is a verb meaning recoil.
explanation.definitionFit: To cower is to crouch or draw back in fear, and to shrink is to recoil in the same way.

clue.text: A piece of bread you prepared

indicators.note: a piece is only a part, so the letters come from a portion of the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the two words, dropping the first and last

explanation.surface: A slice of bread you got ready yourself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prepared' reads as describing the bread, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready and prepared are synonyms meaning in a fit state for action or use.

clue.text: Evil AI running compound

parts.note: HAL 9000, the murderous computer in 2001: A Space Odyssey
a machine that is running is on

explanation.surface: A malevolent artificial intelligence operates a fortified enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compound' suggests a walled site for the rogue AI, but it is a chemical compound.
explanation.definitionFit: A halon is a halogenated hydrocarbon chemical compound, best known for use in fire extinguishers.

clue.text: Poet in with queen

parts.note: someone who is in is at home
R for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A poet in favour with the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In with' reads as being in favour, but 'in' gives a word for being at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer is the ancient Greek poet credited with the epic poems the Iliad and the Odyssey.

clue.text: Conservative let his best man off

definitions.note: the answer is a noun; the definition is an adjective, describing what the establishment is

indicators.note: something off has gone bad or wrong, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the four words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A Tory groom allows his best man to leave early.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a wedding with a Tory in charge; all thirteen letters of the following four words are reshuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: The Establishment is the traditional ruling class, a group inclined to preserve existing institutions and resist change.

clue.text: At party, we upset US lawman

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are tumbled into a new order

parts.note: the three words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A sheriff is put out by the guests at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' looks like distress at the party; it rearranges the letters of the first three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Wyatt Earp was a Wild West marshal famous for the gunfight at the O.K. Corral in Tombstone.
